tasks_completed.description: Added gzip compression directives to nginx config in Dockerfile.webapp
tasks_completed.changes: Inserted gzip on, gzip_vary on, gzip_proxied any, gzip_comp_level 6, gzip_min_length 256, gzip_types (text/plain text/css text/javascript application/javascript application/json application/xml image/svg+xml application/x-javascript text/xml), gzip_static on — all placed inside the server{} block after 'listen 80;' and before the first location block
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause: nginx config was written without gzip directives when Dockerfile.webapp was originally created. Default nginx:alpine has gzip off when default.conf is replaced. Added all 7 directives per BA spec (Must Have + Should Have requirements).

git_rationale.root_cause_commit: N/A - gzip was never configured in the Dockerfile.webapp nginx config
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: Original Dockerfile.webapp focused on SPA routing correctness; gzip compression was overlooked. When custom nginx config replaces default.conf, gzip reverts to nginx's compiled-in default (off).
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Explicitly enables gzip with all relevant directives in the server block. gzip_static on allows serving pre-compressed .gz files if Expo build generates them, with graceful fallback to on-the-fly compression.

dev.qa_notes: After rebuilding happy-app:dev from this worktree and deploying happy-web-dev, verify with: curl -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' -sI http://localhost:8097/ | grep -i content-encoding (expect 'content-encoding: gzip'). Also verify JS bundle: curl -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' -sI http://localhost:8097/_expo/static/js/web/index-*.js | grep -i content-encoding. Image files (PNG/JPEG) should NOT have content-encoding header (already compressed formats are not in gzip_types list).

recommendations: After deploying, confirm transfer size for main JS bundle drops significantly from 7.4MB baseline
If Expo web export generates .gz files alongside originals, gzip_static will serve them with zero CPU cost
